auditedPaper.role: draft derived from v1 pilot evidence

overallAssessment.reason: The draft is numerically traceable to the v1 artifacts, but its central tradeoff and optimizer-discovery language is stronger than the repeated evidence supports. Policy-space identifiability and latency measurement must be corrected before official validation.
overallAssessment.preservationDecision: Keep the v1 paper and raw artifacts as a pilot snapshot. Do not rewrite raw results or present the current optimizer point as seed-stable final evidence.

findings.title: The repeated baseline matrix does not show a p95-versus-node tradeoff

evidence.observation: For cpu-tight, mem-tight, and fragmenting-mix, Packing and Spread both have mean p95=1.6667 s, while Packing uses 2, 2, and 3 occupied workers versus Spread's 4, 4, and 4. Packing weakly dominates Spread on the two reported objectives in every repeated baseline workload.

findings.assessment: The matrix proves that policy weights change placement and consolidation, but it does not by itself prove a conflicting primary-objective surface. The sentence after the fragmenting-mix comparison draws the opposite conclusion from the displayed values.
findings.requiredAction: Use the matrix only as pilot evidence of placement sensitivity. Build v2 workloads and measurements that can produce a repeated latency-consolidation conflict before restoring the tradeoff claim.

findings.title: The nominal four-dimensional policy representation is not identifiable on homogeneous workers

evidence.derivation: For a feasible candidate on homogeneous workers, packing = candidate-independent constant - 0.5*freeCPU - 0.5*freeMem. Node ranking therefore depends on effective coefficients (wCPU-0.5*wPacking), (wMem-0.5*wPacking), and wPod. Positive scaling of all weights also preserves rankings.

findings.assessment: Different four-gene chromosomes may represent the same scheduler policy. Duplicate objective points cannot be interpreted as independent policy discoveries without a ranking-equivalence audit.
findings.requiredAction: Complete Gate 1: add invariance tests, normalize representation scale, and remove or redefine the dependent Packing signal before official optimization.

findings.title: The optimizer-only lower-pending point is numerically real but not robustly validated

evidence.observation: Two candidates have objectives (0.6667, 4.0), and the combined front has two unique points. Each candidate was evaluated once on workloads containing 4, 4, and 6 Pods. Workload-level p95 values for the lower-pending point are 0, 1, and 1 seconds.

findings.assessment: The coordinates and Pareto membership are correctly reported for the single stream, but policy quality is confounded with scheduler cadence, timestamp resolution, and one-shot evaluation noise.
findings.requiredAction: Describe this point as a v1 pilot observation only. Re-evaluate official finalists repeatedly after policy and measurement v2, then test recurrence across seeds.

findings.title: The active-node objective name overstates what is measured

evidence.observation: The evaluator counts distinct worker names hosting non-terminal evaluator-managed Pods at each poll. It does not observe powered, autoscaled, Ready, or billable nodes.

findings.assessment: The detailed methodology defines the metric, but abstract labels and cost-proxy interpretation can be read as infrastructure activation.
findings.requiredAction: Rename it to max workload-occupied worker nodes in v2 artifacts and state separately that it is a consolidation proxy.

findings.title: The v1 workloads create placement pressure, not whole-cluster capacity pressure

evidence.observation: The workloads request totals equivalent to 1.80 worker CPU, 1.80 worker memory, and 1.76 workers in each dimension respectively on a 4-worker cluster. They force multi-node placement but do not saturate aggregate cluster capacity.

findings.assessment: Calling them resource-pressure workloads is acceptable as a project label but can imply queue-producing global saturation that is not present.
findings.requiredAction: Call v1 scenarios placement/consolidation pressure workloads, or make v2 demand and arrival patterns generate measurable queue and capacity pressure.

findings.title: Pending-time wording does not identify the actual timestamp source

evidence.observation: PendingSeconds is CreationTimestamp subtracted from the PodScheduled=True condition LastTransitionTime. It is not measured from the evaluator poll time or directly from the first observed spec.nodeName assignment.

findings.assessment: The current prose is directionally correct but insufficient for reproducing or interpreting sub-second differences.
findings.requiredAction: State the exact condition and timestamp fields, quantify their resolution, and separate scheduler decision latency from evaluator observation latency in measurement v2.

findings.title: Historical run metadata is incomplete and reconstructed

evidence.observation: Execution commits can be inferred with high confidence, but exact commands, dirty state, Kubernetes version, kind version, node image, and Go runtime version were not persisted.

findings.assessment: The reconstructed manifests improve traceability but cannot convert the historical runs into official evidence under the new hard gate.
findings.requiredAction: Capture these fields at run start in official v2 manifests and include the protocol tag or commit in the final paper.

findings.title: Related work and external baseline coverage remain incomplete

evidence.observation: The draft explicitly excludes an experimental default kube-scheduler baseline and contains no standalone related-work synthesis for scheduler optimization and multi-objective search.

findings.assessment: This is disclosed correctly, but it limits external validity and CFP reviewer context.
findings.requiredAction: Add a default kube-scheduler reference protocol and use SciSpace only for discovery, verifying every cited claim against primary papers or official documentation.

verifiedClaims.claim: Packing reduces mean occupied workers from 4 to 2 on cpu-tight and mem-tight.
All nine baseline combinations scheduled and completed all Pods with zero unschedulable count.
The seed-42 optimizer artifact contains 72 evaluated candidates, 75 total measured solutions, four combined nondominated members, and two unique objective points.
Packing survives the seed-42 combined front; Default and Spread are dominated in that stream.
Table and figure values for the baseline means and seed-42 unique points match the committed raw artifacts after rounding.
verifiedClaims.evidence: paper/main.tex and paper/figures/*.tex compared with committed JSON/CSV

verifiedClaims.claim: The paper distinguishes three-repeat baseline means from the single optimizer evaluation stream.

gate0Decision.invalidationCondition: This audit should be superseded, not edited into an official audit, after policy, measurement, workload, baseline, and multi-seed v2 evidence is committed.
